content.text:
The build is green. The implementation is complete.

## Summary

I implemented the per-city capacity rule for owner creation, following the existing count-based conventions in the codebase (mirroring `countOwnersByName`):

1. **`ClinicService.java`** — added `int countOwnersByCity(String city)` to the service interface.

2. **`ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — implemented `countOwnersByCity` as a read-only transactional method that counts existing owners whose city matches case-insensitively (same idiom as `countOwnersByName`).

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, added a check that returns `409 CONFLICT` when the owner's city already contains 50 or more owners, placed alongside the existing conflict checks.

The acceptance test (`coreRejectsWhenCityAtCapacity`, which fills a fresh city to 50 owners then expects the 51st to be rejected) and the full suite pass with `BUILD SUCCESS`.

## Summary

I implemented the per-city capacity rule for owner creation, following the existing count-based conventions in the codebase (mirroring `countOwnersByName`):

1. **`ClinicService.java`** — added `int countOwnersByCity(String city)` to the service interface.

2. **`ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — implemented `countOwnersByCity` as a read-only transactional method that counts existing owners whose city matches case-insensitively (same idiom as `countOwnersByName`).

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, added a check that returns `409 CONFLICT` when the owner's city already contains 50 or more owners, placed alongside the existing conflict checks.

The acceptance test (`coreRejectsWhenCityAtCapacity`, which fills a fresh city to 50 owners then expects the 51st to be rejected) and the full suite pass with `BUILD SUCCESS`.
